# PRD: <feature>

- **Date:** <date>
- **Status:** Draft | Approved (owner and revision)
- **Affected modules:** <modules>
- **Related epic or issue:** <reference or unfiled>

## Goal

State the user outcome in one or two sentences.

## Context and project alignment

Identify the feature's role in JobScout. Cite existing data, contracts and accepted ADRs.

## Dependencies

Carry over every epic prerequisite with its current status. Move unresolved prerequisite conflicts to Open Questions.

## User scenarios

Describe the actor, trigger, existing state, and visible result.

## In scope

Specify the behavior delivered in this iteration.

## Out of scope

Carry over the epic's exclusions and clarify relevant adjacent work.

## Key invariants and variation points

Record what must always hold. Name the policy, provider, format, or pipeline step that can vary and its existing boundary. Write “No variation point” when there is none.

## Technical constraints

List established constraints such as privacy, quotas or supported environments.

## Functional requirements

State behavior and state changes the user can observe.

## Non-functional requirements

Give measurable reliability, usability, latency, security or cost requirements where they matter.

## Acceptance criteria

Give each criterion a stable ID and observable outcome. Preserve all epic criteria and explain any addition.

## Test requirement sketch

Describe the kinds of evidence required. Keep manual owner checks separate.

## Edge cases and failure scenarios

Record missing or ambiguous inputs, duplicates, partial failures, retries and visible recovery.

## Open questions

Assign unresolved decisions to an owner. Resolve material scope and ADR conflicts before approval.

## Documentation to update

Name artifacts affected by contracts, state changes or new architecture.

## Proposed subtask breakdown (epic only)

List candidate topics in dependency order and map each to acceptance criteria. Consider an integration branch for independently testable cross-module phases.
